meaning.en: In a hopelessly tangled mess, like a heap of hemp threads; used of thoughts, affairs or situations.
meaning.zh: 乱得像一团麻线，形容事情或思绪杂乱无章。

equivalents: like a ball of knotted thread

examples.zh: 听到噩耗，她心绪纷乱如麻。
examples.en: On hearing the bad news her thoughts were in a hopeless tangle.

examples.zh: 账目纷乱如麻，会计整整查了三天。
examples.en: The accounts were in a tangled mess, and the accountant spent three whole days sorting them out.

usage.en: Predicate or complement; used of mind and situations alike. A near-synonym is 乱如麻 (a shorter form), and 心乱如麻 is the common fixed phrase for the mind.
usage.zh: 作谓语或补语，可指心绪也可指局面。近义的“乱如麻”较短，“心乱如麻”是描写心绪的常用说法。

natural: a scrap of paper, a single word

meaning.en: A scrap of paper and a single word: the smallest scrap of writing; the tiniest remnant of a text.
meaning.zh: 零碎的纸片和个别的文字，指极少的文字材料。

examples.zh: 他走得匆忙，没有留下片纸只字。
examples.en: He left in a hurry and did not leave a single written word.

examples.zh: 这位作家的片纸只字也被人当作珍宝收藏。
examples.en: Even the smallest scrap written by this author is treasured by collectors.

usage.en: Pinyin: 只 here is zhī ('single'), not zhǐ. Often negated: 不留/没有片纸只字.
usage.zh: 注意“只”读 zhī（单个），不读 zhǐ。常用否定式“不留/没有片纸只字”。

meaning.en: To speak freely and grandly, airing lofty opinions without restraint.
meaning.zh: 毫无顾忌地发表高深议论。

examples.zh: 酒席上，他放言高论，纵论天下大事。
examples.en: At the dinner he held forth at length on the affairs of the world.

examples.zh: 几位学者放言高论，谁也不让谁。
examples.en: Several scholars laid out their views at large, none yielding to another.

usage.en: Neutral to slightly ironic depending on tone; can be admiring (frank, learned) or mocking (grandstanding). Literary.
usage.zh: 视语气而定，可含赞许（直率博学），也可含讽刺（夸夸其谈）。书面语。

meaning.en: A person of extraordinary natural beauty or charm, born to attract attention; traditionally of a woman.
meaning.zh: 天生的绝色美人，多指女子，也指出类拔萃的人物。

examples.zh: 这位女演员被誉为天生尤物，一出场就吸引了所有目光。
examples.en: The actress is called a born beauty and drew every eye as she appeared.

examples.zh: 古书里常把杨贵妃称作天生尤物。
examples.en: Old books often call Yang Guifei a beauty beyond compare.

usage.en: Dated and sometimes objectifying; best kept to historical or literary contexts. 尤物 means 'an outstanding thing or person'.
usage.zh: 略显过时，有时带物化意味，宜用于历史或文学语境。“尤物”指出众的人或物。

meaning.en: A person who seems to belong among the immortals: elegant, detached and free of worldly cares.
meaning.zh: 像神仙一样超凡脱俗的人。

equivalents: a person apart from the mortal world

examples.zh: 他白衣飘飘，气度不凡，宛如神仙中人。
examples.en: In flowing white and with an air of distinction, he seemed one of the immortals.

examples.zh: 众人都说那位老道士是神仙中人。
examples.en: Everyone said the old Daoist was a man out of this world.

usage.en: Praise for grace and detachment; sometimes of good fortune and ease. Often with 宛如/真是. Literary.
usage.zh: 赞美风度超逸、不染尘俗，也可指生活闲适。常与“宛如/真是”搭配。书面语。

meaning.en: Spray flying like pearls and jade, describing the sparkling beauty of waterfalls, rapids and fountains.
meaning.zh: 水珠飞溅如珠玉，形容瀑布、激流或喷泉的壮美。

examples.zh: 瀑布从崖顶倾泻而下，飞珠溅玉，蔚为壮观。
examples.en: The waterfall pours from the cliff top in a dazzling spray, a magnificent sight.

examples.zh: 喷泉在阳光下飞珠溅玉，格外耀眼。
examples.en: The fountain flashes like flying pearls in the sunshine.

usage.en: A poetic description of falling or leaping water; also of lively, polished prose. Literary.
usage.zh: 诗意地描写飞泻或跳跃的水流，也可形容文辞明快华美。书面语。

meaning.en: Rare, beautiful flowers and plants of legend, said to grow in the realm of the immortals; also splendid garden flora.
meaning.zh: 传说中仙境里的奇花异草，也泛指珍奇美丽的花木。

examples.zh: 传说蓬莱仙岛上琪花瑶草，四季不谢。
examples.en: Legend says that on the Isle of Penglai jade-like flowers and herbs never fade.

examples.zh: 园中琪花瑶草，美不胜收。
examples.en: The garden was full of exquisite rare plants, a feast for the eyes.

usage.en: Pinyin: 琪 qí (a kind of jade). Poetic and fantasy-flavoured; used for Daoist paradises or lavish gardens.
usage.zh: “琪”读 qí，是一种美玉。富有诗意和仙境色彩，用于道教仙境或华美花园。

meaning.en: Heroes rising in a time of upheaval: dragons and tigers (outstanding men) meeting wind and cloud (opportunity).
meaning.zh: 龙虎得风云而腾跃，比喻英雄豪杰逢时而起，大有作为。

equivalents: men of destiny in turbulent times

examples.zh: 乱世之中，龙虎风云，群雄并起。
examples.en: In the turmoil of those days, heroes rose from every side.

examples.zh: 这部小说写尽了龙虎风云的时代。
examples.en: The novel captures an age of heroes and upheaval.

usage.en: Describes ambitious men and times of change; often used of rival heroes in historical fiction. Literary.
usage.zh: 形容英雄豪杰和风云变幻的时代，常用于历史小说中群雄争霸。书面语。

meaning.en: To race as fast as the wind and lightning; used of fine horses and of great speed in general.
meaning.zh: 追赶风和闪电，形容速度极快，多用来形容骏马。

examples.zh: 这匹骏马追风逐电，转眼就不见了踪影。
examples.en: This fine horse raced like the wind and was out of sight in an instant.

examples.zh: 高铁追风逐电，几小时就能跨越数省。
examples.en: The high-speed train flashes along and crosses several provinces in a few hours.

usage.en: Positive description of speed; classic of horses and chariots, now also trains and runners. Predicate. Compare 风驰电掣.
usage.zh: 对速度的赞美，原多形容骏马战车，现也用于列车、运动员等。作谓语。可比较“风驰电掣”。

natural: wind and dust all along the road

meaning.en: Wind and dust all the way: the weariness of a long journey.
meaning.zh: 一路上经受风吹尘染，形容旅途劳顿。

examples.zh: 你一路风尘，先歇歇脚再说。
examples.en: You are travel-weary; rest your feet first.

examples.zh: 他带着一路风尘赶到了医院。
examples.en: He arrived at the hospital still covered in the dust of the road.

usage.en: Common in greetings and descriptions of arrivals, as in 一路风尘仆仆 (also 风尘仆仆, the fuller and more usual wording).
usage.zh: 常用于问候和描写抵达，如“一路风尘仆仆”（亦作“风尘仆仆”，更常用）。

meaning.en: Stringed and wind instruments; music in general, especially lively music at a banquet.
meaning.zh: 弦乐器和管乐器，泛指音乐，多指宴席上的热闹乐声。

examples.zh: 宴会上丝竹管弦，歌舞升平。
examples.en: At the banquet there were strings, pipes, song and dance.

examples.zh: 远处传来丝竹管弦之声，悠扬悦耳。
examples.en: From afar came the sound of strings and pipes, melodious and pleasing.

usage.en: From the classical view of instruments by material (silk strings, bamboo pipes). Literary scene-setting for entertainments. Also 管弦丝竹.
usage.zh: 源自古代按材质分类乐器（丝弦、竹管）。书面语，用于渲染宴乐场面。

meaning.en: Not reliable enough to serve as evidence or a basis for judgement.
meaning.zh: 不能作为凭证或依据。

examples.zh: 光凭他一句话，不足为凭。
examples.en: His word alone is not good enough to go on.

examples.zh: 口说无凭，传闻不足为凭。
examples.en: Talk without proof, and rumour, are not to be relied on.

usage.en: Common in argument, law and news writing, often with 空口/传闻/一面之词. Formal and negative in tone about evidence.
usage.zh: 常用于论证、法律和新闻写作，常与“空口/传闻/一面之词”搭配。书面语，对证据持否定态度。

meaning.en: To be willing to die for something without any regret.
meaning.zh: 即使死了也没有怨恨和遗憾。

examples.zh: 只要能救出孩子，我死而无怨。
examples.en: If I can save the child, I would die without regret.

examples.zh: 为了心爱的事业，他死而无怨。
examples.en: For the cause he loved, he would have died with no regrets.

usage.en: Expresses total devotion or sacrifice; often follows 只要/若能... Declarative, formal; a strong statement of loyalty or love.
usage.zh: 表达完全的奉献或牺牲精神，常接在“只要/若能……”之后。语气庄重而强烈。

natural: the fit prevail, the unfit lose

meaning.en: The superior win and the inferior lose: the principle of competition, associated with natural selection.
meaning.zh: 强者、优者取胜，弱者、劣者失败，指竞争的自然法则。

equivalents: the strong win and the weak lose

examples.zh: 市场竞争优胜劣败，企业必须不断创新。
examples.en: Market competition favours the fit and eliminates the weak, so firms must keep innovating.

examples.zh: 自然界遵循优胜劣败的法则。
examples.en: The natural world follows the rule of survival of the fittest.

usage.en: A term from the Chinese rendering of Darwinian ideas (late Qing). Today commonly 优胜劣汰, which is the more usual form in news; 优胜劣败 stresses the result.
usage.zh: 是清末翻译进化论时流行的说法。今天新闻中更常用“优胜劣汰”，“优胜劣败”侧重结果。

meaning.en: To be addicted to drinking and sensual pleasures.
meaning.zh: 沉迷于喝酒和女色。

examples.zh: 这位皇帝沉湎酒色，不理朝政。
examples.en: The emperor, steeped in drink and pleasure, neglected affairs of state.

examples.zh: 他年纪轻轻就沉湎酒色，把家业败光了。
examples.en: He gave himself to dissipation while young and squandered the family estate.

usage.en: Pinyin: 湎 miǎn. Strongly critical; typical of historical writing on dissolute rulers or sons of rich families.
usage.zh: “湎”读 miǎn。批评意味强，多见于史传，指荒淫的君主或富家子弟。

natural: loyalty, filial piety, integrity and duty

meaning.en: The four traditional Confucian virtues: loyalty to the ruler, filial devotion, personal integrity and righteousness.
meaning.zh: 传统儒家伦理的四种美德：忠君、孝亲、守节、重义。

equivalents: loyalty, filial piety, integrity and righteousness

examples.zh: 这部戏传颂的是忠孝节义的故事。
examples.en: This play celebrates stories of loyalty, filial piety, integrity and duty.

examples.zh: 他从小接受忠孝节义的教育。
examples.en: From a young age he was taught the traditional virtues.

usage.en: Describes the old moral code; now sometimes used with historical distance, since 节 once stressed women's chastity and 忠 loyalty to a monarch. Formal.
usage.zh: 指传统伦理道德，现多带历史距离感地使用，因“节”曾强调女子贞节、“忠”指忠于君主。书面语。

meaning.en: Opposing things that nevertheless complement and complete each other.
meaning.zh: 相互对立的事物又相互补充、相互促成。

examples.zh: 动与静相反相成，缺一不可。
examples.en: Movement and stillness are opposites that complete each other, and neither can be spared.

examples.zh: 文章中的详与略相反相成，才有节奏。
examples.en: Detail and brevity in an essay balance each other and give it rhythm.

story.en: Ban Gu on the schools of thought: 'they oppose each other yet all complete each other' (相反而皆相成也).
story.zh: 《汉书·艺文志》：“相反而皆相成也。”

usage.en: Philosophical, formal; used in argument about dialectics and craft. Contrasts with 相辅相成, which stresses mutual help rather than opposition.
usage.zh: 偏哲学色彩，书面语，用于辩证论述和技艺评论。与“相辅相成”不同，强调对立而统一。

natural: human feelings and the ways of the world

meaning.en: The way people feel and behave in society, especially its warmth and coldness.
meaning.zh: 社会上人与人交往的态度和世间的种种情态。

examples.zh: 他阅尽人情世态，对世事早已看淡。
examples.en: Having seen all the ways of the world, he took things lightly.

examples.zh: 这部小说深刻地描写了人情世态。
examples.en: The novel portrays the ways of society with great insight.

usage.en: A noun phrase used to talk about social observation. Often appears after 看透/阅尽/洞悉. Compare 世态炎凉, which stresses fickleness.
usage.zh: 名词性短语，常用于谈社会观察，多接在“看透/阅尽/洞悉”后。可比较强调冷暖无常的“世态炎凉”。

meaning.en: A benevolent and morally upright person; also used as a respectful address to charitable people.
meaning.zh: 有仁德的、品行高尚的人，也用作对善人的尊称。

equivalents: a person of benevolence and virtue

examples.zh: 这场义演吸引了许多仁人君子捐款。
examples.en: The charity show drew many kind-hearted donors.

examples.zh: 他一生行善，被乡里称作仁人君子。
examples.en: He did good all his life and was known in the village as a man of virtue.

usage.en: Respectful, a little old-fashioned; typical of appeals and eulogies (请仁人君子伸出援手). Noun phrase.
usage.zh: 带尊敬意味，略显老派，多见于呼吁和颂辞（请仁人君子伸出援手）。名词性短语。

meaning.en: What is normal and natural in human feelings; to be expected of anyone.
meaning.zh: 人之常情，指人们通常都有的感情和反应。

examples.zh: 思念亲人是人情之常，不必自责。
examples.en: Missing one's family is only natural; you need not blame yourself.

examples.zh: 见利心动，亦是人情之常。
examples.en: To be tempted by gain is also normal human nature.

usage.en: Used to excuse or explain feelings; commonly in the pattern 这是人情之常. Compare the more colloquial 人之常情.
usage.zh: 用来为某种情感或做法开脱、解释，常说“这是人情之常”。可比较更口语化的“人之常情”。

meaning.en: To go back on what one has said; to break one's own promise.
meaning.zh: 不遵守自己说过的话，违背诺言。

examples.zh: 他答应了又反悔，自食其言，大家都不再信任他。
examples.en: He agreed and then backed out, going back on his word, and nobody trusts him now.

examples.zh: 你可别自食其言啊！
examples.en: Don't go back on your word!

usage.en: Different from 自食其果 (reap what one has sown) and 自食其力 (support oneself); the object is 'one's own words'. Negative, in formal or colloquial speech.
usage.zh: 不同于“自食其果”“自食其力”，所食的是“自己说过的话”。贬义，口语书面语皆可用。

natural: not knowing when to advance or retreat

meaning.en: To lack a sense of propriety or moderation; to not know where to stop.
meaning.zh: 不懂得分寸，不知道什么时候该进、什么时候该退。

examples.zh: 对领导这样说话，未免太不知进退了。
examples.en: Speaking to the boss like that shows no sense of limits.

examples.zh: 他不知进退，一再纠缠别人。
examples.en: He does not know when to stop and keeps pestering others.

usage.en: Criticises tactlessness or overreach; often follows 太/真是. Can also be used in a milder sense of lacking tact. Compare 进退有度 (the opposite).
usage.zh: 批评不懂分寸、过分冒进，常接“太/真是”。可比较反义的“进退有度”。

meaning.en: To act against one's conscience, doing wrong knowingly while pretending not to.
meaning.zh: 违背良心，明知故犯而自欺欺人。

examples.zh: 做瞒心昧己的事，终究会良心不安。
examples.en: One who acts against his conscience will never be at ease.

examples.zh: 他明知账目有假，还瞒心昧己地签了字。
examples.en: Knowing the accounts were false, he signed them against his conscience.

usage.en: Pinyin: 昧 mèi. Literary; moral criticism, used with 做/干 + 瞒心昧己的事. Compare 昧着良心.
usage.zh: “昧”读 mèi。书面语，道德批评，常说“做/干瞒心昧己的事”。可比较“昧着良心”。
